doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Chez Nicki Jams cooking-and-music web series for World Central Kitchen
summary: Monk opens; Nicki explains the online series started as a joke with her husband Brian and stepson Andrew, raising money for World Central Kitchen.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m happy to have my guest Nicki Parrott here today, remotely unfortunately, but I did think it was worth gathering some stories for the Fillius Jazz Archive about how musicians and artists are making out these days. And we’ve seen some very upbeat examples of how you’re making out with your new online adventure and really enjoying Chez Nicki Jams.

Thank you. I’m so glad you are. I’ve had some really nice feedback from it because it feels like an escape but it’s also supporting a good cause, the World Central Kitchen, and they are needed right now. They are world-wide. They were helping in Australia when the bush fires were in Australia in January of this year and they’re helping out during the pandemic, you know, countless meals everyday, hoping to keep restaurants open to cook the meals for families. So that’s nice. It’s sort of — it started because we were all here and you know I haven’t had a gig since March 12 I think was the last gig. I cut a European tour short. And you know all three of us sitting here — Andrew is here from — my stepson — is here from San Francisco. He works at Apple. Also closed. So he has certain technology/computer skills. Brian has audio recording and video skills which he needs for his work. We are all working from home. And I’m here kind of playing and doing a little online teaching. But I’ve been cooking a lot. And it sort of started as a joke, “Why don’t you make pineapple pizza and we’ll film it and then you play a song?” I’m like, “Naa, that would never work.” And so I thought well let’s try it. If it’s fun we’ll do it. And it was fun. We did one episode and we said well let’s do it weekly for a while. We’ve committed to six. We just filmed number five, we’ve aired number four. And then we’ll promote it at a time that feels right. We’ll do the six, put them aside, and then figure out — we’ve made some money. It’s a good cause, good charity, and we’ll see what happens next with it you know. But it’s fun and it puts all our skills to use so it’s been a good thing to do together.
